key_partners.ideal: An ideal partner network brings strategic capabilities, co-innovation, and access to unique assets or markets that would be hard to build internally.
key_partners.anti_ideal: Partnerships are generic, transactional, or redundant—offering no strategic value or differentiation from competitors.

key_activities.ideal: Key activities are focused, innovative, and directly tied to delivering unique value—often leveraging proprietary methods or technology.
key_activities.anti_ideal: Activities are routine, operationally bloated, or irrelevant to the core value proposition—offering no competitive edge.

key_resources.ideal: The business leverages unique and hard-to-replicate resources—such as proprietary technology, brand equity, or specialized talent.
key_resources.anti_ideal: Resources are generic, easily available in the market, and do not contribute to any unique capability or advantage.

value_propositions.ideal: A compelling and differentiated value proposition that solves real problems in a novel way and creates measurable customer impact.
value_propositions.anti_ideal: A vague, undifferentiated offering that mimics existing solutions and fails to resonate with customer needs.

customer_relationships.ideal: Customer relationships are personalized, trust-based, and continuously enhanced using data and feedback.
customer_relationships.anti_ideal: Interactions are impersonal, transactional, or inconsistent—resulting in low customer retention or engagement.

channels.ideal: Channels are integrated, customer-centric, and optimized for convenience, efficiency, and brand coherence.
channels.anti_ideal: Channels are fragmented, outdated, or disconnected from how customers actually prefer to interact.

revenue_streams.ideal: Revenue streams are diversified, recurring, and aligned with the value delivered—enabling long-term sustainability.
revenue_streams.anti_ideal: Revenues are one-off, unreliable, or misaligned with customer value, making growth and sustainability difficult.

customer_segments.ideal: The business serves clearly defined, high-potential segments with tailored offerings and deep understanding of their needs.
customer_segments.anti_ideal: Customer segments are too broad, poorly defined, or selected without insight—leading to diluted focus and weak fit.

key_resources.anti_ideal: Resources are misused, unsustainable, or exploitative—damaging long-term value and stakeholder trust.

value_propositions.anti_ideal: Adds no meaningful value or may even harm users, communities, or the environment.

customer_segments.anti_ideal: Focuses only on short-term profits from overexploited, saturated, or vulnerable segments without regard for equity or need.
